cause: Highly contagious FMD virus causes blisters on mouth, tongue, gums, and between hooves. Spreads fast through direct contact, air, feed, and equipment.
warning: Notifiable disease in most countries, report to local veterinary/animal husbandry department immediately. No cure, only supportive care and outbreak control.

medicines.name: Supportive antibiotics (for secondary infection)
medicines.note: No specific antiviral cure, treats secondary bacterial infection only

topical_treatments.name: Potassium permanganate solution
topical_treatments.use: Wash mouth and hoof lesions 2x daily to prevent secondary infection

supplements.name: Multivitamin + Mineral Mix (Cattle)
supplements.benefit: General immune and healing support, replaces nutrients lost during illness

safety_warnings: Isolate affected animal immediately, highly contagious to other cattle
Vaccinate herd regularly in endemic areas
Restrict movement of animals and people from infected farm
Milk from infected cow should not be given raw to calves or consumed

cause: Bacterial infection of the udder (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, E. coli) usually from poor milking hygiene, injury, or dirty bedding.
warning: Severe cases (hot, hard, painful udder with fever) can become toxic mastitis, a life-threatening emergency needing immediate vet care.

medicines.name: Intramammary Antibiotic Infusion (Cephalosporin-based)
medicines.dose: As per vet, infused into affected quarter after milking
medicines.note: Follow milk withdrawal period strictly before selling milk

topical_treatments.name: Warm compress on udder
topical_treatments.use: Apply warm cloth 10-15 min before milking to ease pain and improve milk flow

supplements.name: Vitamin E + Selenium Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports udder tissue health and immune response during infection

safety_warnings: Milk from treated quarter must be discarded during withdrawal period, do not sell or feed to calves
Strip out infected milk fully at each milking, do not let it sit in udder
Maintain clean, dry bedding to prevent recurrence

cause: Excess gas trapped in the rumen from eating too much lush legume pasture, grain overload, or blocked esophagus, causing visible left-side belly swelling.
warning: Severe bloat can compress the lungs and heart causing death within an hour, this is an emergency needing immediate action.

medicines.name: Anti-bloat drench (Poloxalene or vegetable oil)
medicines.dose: As per vet weight-based dosing, drenched orally
medicines.note: Severe cases need vet to pass a stomach tube or perform emergency rumen puncture (trocarization)

supplements.name: Rumen Probiotic/Yeast Culture
supplements.benefit: Restores healthy rumen microbes and digestion after illness or treatment

safety_warnings: If cow is struggling to breathe and collapsing, this is a life-threatening emergency, call vet immediately
Avoid sudden access to lush wet legume pasture (clover, alfalfa)
Never leave bloated cattle unattended

cause: Sudden drop in blood calcium level around calving time, as huge calcium demand goes into milk production, common in high-yielding dairy cows.
warning: Cow becomes unable to stand, weak, and can develop bloat or die if untreated, needs emergency calcium therapy.

medicines.name: Calcium Borogluconate 23% IV/SC
medicines.dose: As per vet, given slowly IV while monitoring heart
medicines.note: Give slowly, too fast IV calcium can cause fatal heart problems

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 + Calcium Bolus
supplements.benefit: Supports calcium absorption and bone/muscle function around calving

safety_warnings: Down cow unable to rise after calving needs vet attention same day
Feed a proper pre-calving (dry period) diet to reduce risk
Do not force a down cow to stand roughly, support gently

cause: Energy deficiency in early lactation when milk production demand exceeds feed intake, body breaks down fat rapidly producing ketones.
warning: Cow shows reduced appetite, weight loss, and sweet/acetone smell on breath, can progress to nervous signs if untreated.

medicines.name: Propylene Glycol Drench
medicines.dose: As per vet, drenched daily for 3-5 days
medicines.note: Dextrose IV may be needed by vet in severe cases

supplements.name: Niacin (Vitamin B3) Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports energy metabolism and reduces fat breakdown in early lactation

safety_warnings: Ensure proper energy-dense feeding in transition period before and after calving
Avoid sudden feed changes around calving
Persistent off-feed cows need vet bloodwork to confirm diagnosis

cause: Bacterial infection (Fusobacterium necrophorum) enters through skin between the claws, often from wet, muddy, or unhygienic ground conditions.
warning: Untreated foot rot can spread to joints and bone causing permanent lameness, treat early.

medicines.name: Oxytetracycline Injection
medicines.note: Follow meat/milk withdrawal period

topical_treatments.name: Copper Sulfate Foot Bath
topical_treatments.use: Walk cattle through foot bath regularly to prevent and treat foot rot

supplements.name: Zinc + Biotin Hoof Supplement
supplements.benefit: Strengthens hoof horn and skin, supports faster healing of foot lesions

safety_warnings: Keep walking areas dry and clean to prevent foot rot
Isolate and treat lame animals promptly to prevent spread
Trim overgrown hooves regularly

cause: Lumpy Skin Disease virus spread by biting insects (flies, mosquitoes, ticks), causes firm round skin nodules all over the body.
warning: Notifiable disease in most regions, can cause major milk drop and economic loss, vaccination is the main prevention.

medicines.name: Supportive antibiotics (for secondary skin infection)
medicines.note: No specific antiviral cure available, supportive care only

topical_treatments.name: Antiseptic wound spray for nodules
topical_treatments.use: Apply to open or ulcerated nodules to prevent fly strike and secondary infection

supplements.name: Multivitamin Immune Support Mix
supplements.benefit: General immune support and nutrient replacement during viral illness

safety_warnings: Vaccinate herd annually in endemic areas
Control biting flies and ticks around cattle sheds
Report suspected cases to local veterinary authority

cause: Brucella bacteria causing abortion in late pregnancy, retained placenta, and infertility, spread through contact with infected birth fluids or milk.
warning: Zoonotic disease, can infect humans (undulant fever) through unpasteurized milk or handling infected birth material, wear gloves.

supplements.name: General Nutrition/Mineral Mix
supplements.benefit: Maintains basic nutrition and mineral balance, supportive only, does not treat the disease

safety_warnings: No effective treatment in cattle, infected animals are usually culled per government policy
Never drink unpasteurized milk from an unvaccinated/untested herd
Vaccinate calves as per national brucellosis control program
Wear gloves when handling aborted fetus or afterbirth

cause: Bacillus anthracis bacteria from contaminated soil, often causes sudden death with bleeding from natural body openings, no time for symptoms in acute cases.
warning: Zoonotic and notifiable disease, do NOT open or perform post-mortem on a suspected anthrax carcass, spores contaminate ground for decades.

medicines.name: Penicillin (early/suspected cases only)
medicines.dose: As per vet, only if caught before sudden death
medicines.note: Often too late as death can be sudden, prevention via vaccination is key

safety_warnings: Never cut open a carcass suspected of anthrax, report to vet/authorities immediately
Bury or burn carcass deeply as directed by authorities, do not skin or handle
Vaccinate herds annually in endemic areas
Extremely dangerous to humans, avoid all direct contact with suspect carcass

cause: Clostridium bacteria spores in soil enter through wounds or are ingested, cause gas gangrene in large muscles, mostly affects young cattle 6 months-2 years.
warning: Rapidly fatal, affected muscle feels crackly (gas under skin) and animal is severely lame with high fever, often found dead.

medicines.name: High-dose Penicillin
medicines.dose: As per vet, only effective if caught very early
medicines.note: Disease often progresses too fast for treatment to succeed

safety_warnings: Vaccinate young cattle annually, this is the main effective prevention
Do not open carcass without vet guidance, spores contaminate pasture
Report sudden deaths in young cattle to vet for diagnosis

cause: Pasteurella multocida bacterial infection, often triggered by stress (transport, monsoon, overcrowding), causes high fever, throat swelling, and rapid death.
warning: Can kill within 24 hours of first signs, throat/neck swelling with difficulty breathing is a medical emergency.

medicines.name: Oxytetracycline or Sulfonamide Injection
medicines.dose: As per vet, early treatment critical
medicines.note: Must be started at first sign of fever for best chance of survival

supplements.name: Electrolyte + Glucose Oral Drench
supplements.benefit: Prevents dehydration and energy crash when appetite/water intake drops

safety_warnings: Vaccinate before monsoon season in endemic areas, this disease often flares with rain
Reduce transport stress and overcrowding
Isolate sick animals immediately, highly contagious

cause: Bacterial (E. coli, Salmonella), viral (Rotavirus, Coronavirus), or parasitic (Cryptosporidia) infection in young calves, worsened by poor colostrum intake.
warning: Calves dehydrate very fast, severe scours can kill within 24-48 hours if untreated, this is an emergency in young calves.

medicines.name: Oral/IV Electrolyte Fluid Therapy
medicines.dose: As per vet, frequent small amounts or IV in severe dehydration
medicines.note: Fluid therapy is the most important treatment, more critical than antibiotics

supplements.name: Oral Rehydration Salts for Calves
supplements.benefit: Replaces fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhea, critical in young calves

supplements.name: Calf Probiotic Powder
supplements.benefit: Restores healthy gut bacteria after diarrhea and antibiotic treatment

safety_warnings: Ensure calf receives adequate colostrum within first 6 hours of birth to build immunity
Severely weak or unable-to-stand calves need emergency vet IV fluids
Keep calving area clean and dry to reduce infection risk

cause: Bacterial or viral respiratory infection, often triggered by cold weather, poor ventilation, overcrowding, or transport stress.
warning: Rapid or labored breathing with fever needs prompt treatment, can progress to fatal lung damage if delayed.

medicines.name: Oxytetracycline or Florfenicol Injection
medicines.note: Follow milk/meat withdrawal period strictly

supplements.name: Cod Liver Oil / Vitamin A+D Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports respiratory tissue healing and general immunity

safety_warnings: Ensure good ventilation and dry bedding in cattle sheds
Isolate coughing animals to reduce spread
Vaccinate calves against common respiratory pathogens where available

cause: Blood parasites (Babesia or Theileria) transmitted by tick bites, destroy red blood cells causing fever, weakness, and dark red-brown urine.
warning: Red-brown urine with high fever is a medical emergency, severe anemia can be fatal without prompt treatment.

medicines.name: Imidocarb Dipropionate or Buparvaquone
medicines.dose: As per vet based on species of parasite and severity
medicines.note: Different drugs used for Babesia vs Theileria, vet diagnosis needed

topical_treatments.name: Tick control spray/pour-on for herd
topical_treatments.use: Apply regularly per label to prevent tick infestation

supplements.name: Iron + Vitamin B12 Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports red blood cell recovery after anemia from blood parasite damage

safety_warnings: Regular tick control is the best prevention
Dark red-brown urine in cattle needs same-day vet attention
New animals introduced to herd should be checked and treated for ticks

cause: Placenta fails to expel within 12-24 hours after calving, due to calcium deficiency, difficult calving, infection, or nutritional issues.
warning: Retained placenta left too long can cause severe uterine infection (metritis) and toxic illness, needs vet attention if not passed within 24 hours.

medicines.name: Antibiotic uterine bolus/injection
medicines.note: Manual removal only performed by vet, never pull placenta forcefully at home

supplements.name: Calcium/Phosphorus Mineral Bolus
supplements.benefit: Supports uterine muscle contraction and mineral balance around calving

safety_warnings: Never forcefully pull on retained placenta, can cause uterine damage and severe bleeding
Watch for fever, foul discharge, or off-feed signs indicating infection
Call vet if placenta is not passed within 24 hours

cause: The abomasum (true stomach) fills with gas and shifts out of normal position, usually left side, common in high-producing dairy cows shortly after calving.
warning: Cow goes off feed with reduced milk and a hollow 'ping' sound heard on the flank, needs vet diagnosis and often surgical correction.

medicines.name: Vet-directed surgical correction
medicines.note: Medical rolling technique may be tried by vet in early mild cases, but surgery is often needed

supplements.name: Rumen Probiotic/Yeast Culture
supplements.benefit: Restores healthy rumen microbes and digestion after illness or treatment

safety_warnings: Off-feed cow after calving with reduced milk needs prompt vet exam
Proper transition period feeding reduces risk
Do not delay, condition worsens the longer it is untreated

cause: Trichophyton fungus causes circular grey-white crusty patches of hair loss, spreads through direct contact and shared equipment, common in young/housed cattle.
warning: Zoonotic, can spread to humans especially children handling the animal, wear gloves.

topical_treatments.name: Iodine-based Antifungal Solution
topical_treatments.use: Apply to affected patches daily until healed

supplements.name: Zinc + Biotin Hoof Supplement
supplements.benefit: Strengthens hoof horn and skin, supports faster healing of foot lesions

safety_warnings: Zoonotic, wear gloves when treating and wash hands after contact
Disinfect brushes, halters and shared equipment
Isolate affected animal from herd during treatment

cause: Moraxella bovis bacteria infection of the eye, worsened by flies, dust, and bright sunlight, causes watery eyes, redness, and corneal ulcers.
warning: Untreated cases can progress to a white corneal scar or permanent blindness in the affected eye.

medicines.name: Oxytetracycline Eye Spray/Injection
medicines.note: Long-acting antibiotic injection often used alongside eye treatment

topical_treatments.name: Antibiotic Eye Ointment
topical_treatments.use: Apply directly to affected eye as per vet direction

supplements.name: Vitamin A Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports eye tissue health and healing of corneal irritation

safety_warnings: Control flies around the herd, they spread infection between animals
Isolate severely affected animals
Provide shade to reduce sunlight irritation to eyes

cause: Bovine Papillomavirus causes wart growths usually on head, neck, and shoulders, most common in young cattle, spreads through direct contact.
warning: Usually harmless and self-resolving within a few months as the immune system matures, but large warts obstructing eyes/mouth need vet attention.

supplements.name: Multivitamin Immune Support Mix
supplements.benefit: General immune support and nutrient replacement during viral illness

safety_warnings: Most warts regress on their own within 1-6 months without treatment
Do not attempt to cut off warts at home, risk of bleeding and infection
Isolate heavily affected young cattle from herd to reduce spread

cause: Fasciola parasites ingested from contaminated wet pasture or water, migrate to liver causing damage, weight loss, and reduced milk production.
warning: Chronic infection causes bottle jaw (fluid swelling under jaw) and severe weight loss if untreated for a long time.

medicines.name: Triclabendazole
medicines.note: Follow milk withdrawal period strictly

supplements.name: Liver Tonic Supplement (Herbal)
supplements.benefit: Supports liver detoxification and regeneration after fluke or toxin damage

safety_warnings: Avoid grazing on waterlogged or marshy pasture where fluke snails live
Deworm on a regular schedule as advised by vet in fluke-endemic areas
Bottle jaw swelling under chin is a sign to get vet fecal testing done

cause: Roundworms and other intestinal parasites picked up from contaminated pasture, cause diarrhea, weight loss, poor coat, and reduced growth, mostly in young cattle.
warning: Heavy infestation in young calves can cause severe anemia and stunted growth if not treated regularly.

medicines.name: Albendazole or Ivermectin
medicines.note: Follow milk/meat withdrawal period, rotate dewormer classes to prevent resistance

supplements.name: Multivitamin + Mineral Mix (Cattle)
supplements.benefit: General immune and healing support, replaces nutrients lost during illness

safety_warnings: Follow a regular deworming schedule, especially for young cattle on pasture
Rotate grazing areas to reduce parasite buildup
Do not overdose, weigh animal accurately for correct dosing

cause: Certain plants or liver damage cause a photo-reactive compound to build up in skin, leading to severe sunburn-like reaction on white or light-skinned areas.
warning: Often linked to underlying liver disease or toxic plant ingestion, needs vet evaluation to find and remove the cause.

medicines.name: Anti-inflammatory (vet-prescribed)
medicines.note: Treats pain and inflammation while underlying cause is identified

topical_treatments.name: Zinc oxide skin cream
topical_treatments.use: Apply to affected light-skinned areas to protect from further sun damage

supplements.name: Liver Tonic Supplement (Herbal)
supplements.benefit: Supports liver detoxification and regeneration after fluke or toxin damage

supplements.name: Vitamin E + Selenium Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports udder tissue health and immune response during infection

safety_warnings: Move affected animal to shade immediately
Identify and remove toxic plants from pasture
Vet check needed to rule out liver disease as underlying cause

cause: Cow accidentally swallows a sharp metal object (nail, wire) with feed, which pierces the stomach wall (reticulum) and can damage the heart or other organs.
warning: Sharp pain when moving, hunched back, and reluctance to move can indicate a metal object has pierced internal organs, needs urgent vet care.

medicines.name: Antibiotic + Rumen Magnet (vet-administered)
medicines.note: Magnet given orally to trap metal objects and prevent further migration

supplements.name: Rumen Probiotic/Yeast Culture
supplements.benefit: Restores healthy rumen microbes and digestion after illness or treatment

safety_warnings: Keep feeding areas free of wire, nails, and metal debris
Cow standing hunched with grunting and reluctance to move needs same-day vet exam
Preventive rumen magnets can be given to at-risk herds

cause: Cow is unable to rise despite being alert, often following milk fever, calving injury, nerve damage, or severe metabolic disease.
warning: The longer a cow stays down, the more muscle and nerve damage occurs, urgent vet diagnosis of the underlying cause is essential.

medicines.name: Treatment depends on underlying cause (vet diagnosis required)
medicines.note: Calcium therapy, anti-inflammatory, or nerve support depending on cause found by vet

supplements.name: Calcium-Magnesium-Phosphorus Mix
supplements.benefit: Supports nerve, muscle, and bone function during recovery from a down episode

safety_warnings: Provide soft, dry bedding and turn the cow side to side every few hours to prevent pressure sores
Do not drag a down cow by legs or tail, causes further injury
Get vet diagnosis promptly as cause determines the correct treatment

cause: Bacterial infection entering through the umbilical cord shortly after birth, often due to unhygienic calving conditions, can spread to joints and internal organs.
warning: Can progress to joint infection (joint ill) causing severe lameness and swollen joints in the calf if untreated early.

medicines.name: Antibiotic Injection
medicines.note: Early treatment prevents spread to joints and organs

topical_treatments.name: Iodine Navel Dip
topical_treatments.use: Dip calf's navel cord within hours of birth to prevent infection

supplements.name: Multivitamin Immune Support Mix
supplements.benefit: General immune support and nutrient replacement during viral illness

safety_warnings: Dip every newborn calf's navel in iodine within hours of birth as routine prevention
Keep calving pens clean and dry
Swollen painful navel or joints in a calf needs prompt vet attention

cause: Eimeria protozoa parasite damages the intestinal lining of young calves, especially in crowded or unhygienic housing, causing bloody diarrhea and straining.
warning: Severe cases cause significant blood loss and dehydration in calves, needs prompt treatment and supportive fluids.

medicines.name: Sulfadimethoxine or Amprolium
medicines.note: Complete full course to fully clear infection

supplements.name: Oral Rehydration Salts for Calves
supplements.benefit: Replaces fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhea, critical in young calves

safety_warnings: Keep calf housing clean and dry, overcrowding increases risk
Isolate affected calves to reduce spread to healthy ones
Bloody diarrhea in calves needs prompt vet attention

cause: Clostridium tetani bacteria enters through deep wounds (castration, dehorning, nail injury) and produces a toxin causing severe muscle stiffness and spasms.
warning: Progresses to full body rigidity, inability to eat, and death from respiratory failure if untreated, needs immediate vet care at first sign of stiffness.

medicines.name: Tetanus Antitoxin + Penicillin
medicines.dose: As per vet, given as early as possible
medicines.note: Antitoxin neutralizes circulating toxin, antibiotic kills the bacteria

supplements.name: General Nutrition/Mineral Mix
supplements.benefit: Maintains basic nutrition and mineral balance, supportive only, does not treat the disease

safety_warnings: Vaccinate against tetanus before procedures like castration or dehorning in endemic areas
Keep wounds clean and treat promptly to prevent bacterial entry
Stiff gait, flared nostrils, or protruding third eyelid are early warning signs needing urgent vet exam

cause: Low blood magnesium level, common in cattle grazing lush young spring pasture with low magnesium content, especially in lactating cows.
warning: Causes muscle twitching, staggering, convulsions, and can be rapidly fatal, this is a medical emergency needing immediate calcium/magnesium therapy.

medicines.name: Calcium-Magnesium Borogluconate IV
medicines.dose: As per vet, given slowly IV under close monitoring
medicines.note: Handle animal calmly and quietly, excitement can trigger fatal convulsions

supplements.name: Magnesium Oxide Mineral Supplement
supplements.benefit: Helps prevent and correct low blood magnesium during high-risk grazing periods

safety_warnings: Provide magnesium supplementation before turning cattle onto lush spring pasture
Handle a suspected grass tetany animal calmly and quietly, stress can trigger fatal seizures
Convulsing or staggering cattle need emergency vet care immediately

cause: Actinomyces bacteria enters through injury to the mouth (from sharp feed or foreign objects) and infects the jaw bone, causing a hard, slow-growing swelling.
warning: Untreated infection can prevent normal eating and cause severe weight loss, early treatment gives the best chance of recovery.

medicines.name: Sodium Iodide IV or Long-course Penicillin
medicines.dose: As per vet, often needs weeks of treatment
medicines.note: Early cases respond better, advanced bony swelling is harder to resolve

supplements.name: Multivitamin Immune Support Mix
supplements.benefit: General immune support and nutrient replacement during viral illness

safety_warnings: Any hard, slow-growing jaw swelling needs vet examination to confirm diagnosis
Provide soft feed if chewing is difficult during treatment
Remove sharp or spiky feed material that can injure the mouth

cause: High environmental temperature and humidity overwhelm the cow's ability to cool itself, especially in high-producing dairy cows, causing reduced feed intake and heavy panting.
warning: Severe heat stress can cause collapse and death, especially in transported or poorly ventilated cattle, needs urgent cooling.

topical_treatments.name: Cool water spray/sprinkler system
topical_treatments.use: Spray cool water on the body combined with fanning to lower body temperature

supplements.name: Electrolyte Mineral Mix for Cattle
supplements.benefit: Replaces minerals and fluids lost through heavy panting and reduced intake in hot weather

supplements.name: Vitamin C Supplement
supplements.benefit: Supports immune function and stress recovery during heat stress or illness

safety_warnings: Provide constant access to fresh cool water and shade in hot weather
Avoid transporting or working cattle during the hottest part of the day
Heavy open-mouth panting with drooling is a sign of severe heat stress needing urgent cooling
